skills.title: Finding Early Societies on Maps
skills.description: Early societies, like a First Nation and an Inuit society, lived in different places. Find them on a map and pick what climate and land maps tell about them.

skills.title: Clues from Art and Artefacts
skills.description: Carvings, masks, beadwork, tools, and pottery show how people lived long ago. Pick what each picture of an object tells about daily life.

skills.title: Land, Floods, and Food
skills.description: Rivers, floods, volcanoes, tundra, and changing seasons affected how early societies got food. Match each feature or event to how it helped or hurt.

skills.title: Meeting Needs from the Land
skills.description: Early societies got food, shelter, and clothing from the place where they lived. Match each environment to how people met their needs.

skills.title: Daily Life in Early Societies
skills.description: Early societies had their own food, homes, clothes, school, fun, ceremonies, and ways of travelling. Match each one to its society.

skills.title: Old Inventions and Discoveries
skills.description: People long ago invented calendars, the printing press, farming tools, and better boats. Match each invention to the society that made it and what it did.

skills.title: How Early Societies Were Governed
skills.description: Some early societies had emperors, kings, chiefs, or early democracies. Match each society to who made its rules.

skills.title: Who Was Who in Early Societies
skills.description: Early societies had groups like nobles, peasants, slaves, priests, and merchants. Match each group to its job and how important it was.

skills.title: Comparing How Societies Were Organized
skills.description: Some societies had social classes, inherited privilege, or matrilineal families. Sort what is the same and what is different between societies, and with Canada today.

skills.title: Lives of Different Groups
skills.description: A lord and a serf, or a man and a woman, lived very differently. Match each group's work, food, and home to its place in society.

skills.title: Growing Up Long Ago
skills.description: Young people long ago had different family life, school, play, and chores depending on their background. Sort what is like your life and what is different.

skills.title: Caring for Nature Then and Now
skills.description: Early societies followed seasons and used land and resources in different ways. Sort what is the same and what is different from Canada today.

skills.title: Why Groups Worked Together or Fought
skills.description: Groups cooperated or clashed to trade, explore, win land, gain power, or protect beliefs. Match each reason to an example.

skills.title: Making Peace Long Ago
skills.description: Early societies made peace with ideas like the Great Law of Peace, the Magna Carta, treaties, and shared food. Match each one to how it helped people get along.

skills.title: Canada's Physical Regions
skills.description: Canada has regions like the Western Cordillera, boreal forest, tundra, and the Prairies. Match each region to where it is and what it is like.

skills.title: What People Do in Each Region
skills.description: People farm, mine, fish, ski, and hike in different regions of Canada. Match each activity to the region where it happens.

skills.title: Four Kinds of Industry
skills.description: Industries are resource, manufacturing, service, or information based. Sort jobs like logging, car making, banking, and research into the right sector.

skills.title: Kinds of Political Regions
skills.description: Canada has provinces, territories, municipalities, and First Nations lands. Pick how they are alike and different.

skills.title: Provinces, Territories, and Capitals
skills.description: Match each province and territory to its capital city, where it is, and some of the people who live there.

skills.title: Intermediate Directions and Grids
skills.description: NE, NW, SE, and SW are directions between north, south, east, and west. Use them and map grids to find places in Canada.

skills.title: Opportunities and Challenges by Region
skills.description: Some places have many jobs, while others face job loss, pollution, or crowded cities. Match each region to its good and hard things.

skills.title: Nature Shapes Industry
skills.description: The Shield led to mining, the Maritimes to fishing, and the Prairies to big farms. Match each region's nature to the industry it allows.

skills.title: How Industry Affects Nature
skills.description: Oil sands, dams, mining, fishing, and shipping can change land, air, and water. Match each industry to the effect it has.

skills.title: Using Resources Wisely
skills.description: Companies and people can use solar panels, clean up waste, hunt and fish responsibly, and ask Indigenous communities for input. Pick the actions and how well they help.
